### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `499d445f9939c205ed1ecf51880c50fde0c53d0d` — the merge of head `4c3ef9cef48085a1baaa97a15fbe50c8e70c5b15` into base `efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 499d445f9939c205ed1ecf51880c50fde0c53d0d && git checkout 499d445f9939c205ed1ecf51880c50fde0c53d0d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815 4c3ef9cef48085a1baaa97a15fbe50c8e70c5b15 && git checkout -B drift-repro efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815 && git merge --no-ff 4c3ef9cef48085a1baaa97a15fbe50c8e70c5b15

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json efcbac73cc58510278b970949ac3b65cb9712815
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4c3ef9cef48085a1baaa97a15fbe50c8e70c5b15`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22804 (body and its four comments: triage `6107327152`, claim `6108491444`, `os-dev-report` `6109045625`, ACCEPT `6109072386`), PR #22836 (body, the 5-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge base `b7cd1af9d`), and the check-runs on the head. Read-only: the diff and the tree at the head and at `origin/main` were read with `git show` / `git grep`; nothing was built, run or re-run. The card is labelled `security`, so this record names classes and positions only.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of the redeliver door narrows — right.** `POST /api/v1/webhooks/redeliver` and the `webhooks` slot's `handleRedeliver` now answer `409 DELIVERY_NOT_ELIGIBLE` for a finished delivery whose `sys_webhook` row has `active !== true`, where before the veto let it through; the row is left as it was. This is the triage reading of record on the card (an explicit replay is "the dispatcher" for `active`), it adds a refusal to an existing ledger code, and it sends nothing new: ruling `5271033283`'s non-negotiable half (no operator action sends an unsigned delivery) is untouched. Position: `redeliver-guard.ts:127` at the head; door pins on both faces in `webhook-redeliver-member.test.ts` (the new describe, plus a row in the every-refusal table and the member/mount byte-parity table).
2. **A null or absent `active` is refused — right, and it is the consistent reading, not merely the fail-closed one.** The predicate is `active !== true`, which is exactly what automatic dispatch uses: `auto-enqueuer.ts:393` loads `{ where: { active: true } }`, so such a row is never dispatched on any driver, and a replay that sent it would make the field's own sentence false for that row. Such a row is also unreachable through the engine: the field is `required: true, defaultValue: true` (`sys-webhook.object.ts:175`–`181`), the engine's insert resolves `defaultValue` (objectql `engine.ts`, the `[#4633]` note), and the declared-webhook bootstrap always writes a boolean (`bootstrap-declared-webhooks.ts:349`, `active: wh.isActive !== false`). The guard's read has no projection (`{ where: { id } }` only), so the column is present on every row it sees. Noted, not a conflict: core's `isRowActive` (`packages/core/src/security/row-active.ts`) reads an absent `active` as ACTIVE for the RBAC catalogues; its reason (a mass revocation on deployed rows) does not transfer here, because the dispatcher already skips these rows and the refusal names the remedy.
3. **Check order (gone → inactive → secret) — right.** The gone and unrecoverable-secret refusals keep their text and their order; the inactive check sits between them, so the secret resolver is never called for an inactive row (pinned: resolver call count 0). The only observable change inside the already-refused set is the reason text for a row that is both inactive and key-less, which now names the first remedy; status and code are unchanged, so no accept set moves there.
4. **Public TypeScript surface unchanged — right.** `createWebhookRedeliverGuard` is not re-exported from `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`'s `.` or `./schema` entry (`src/index.ts` names it nowhere; the package `exports` map has only those two subpaths), and the function's signature and return type are unchanged. The changeset's "No code, status, field or export changes" is accurate: the published change is behavioural, at the door.
5. **The refusal string — right.** A runtime string, it carries no tracker number (the `[#22804]` markers are in comments and docblocks only), names the webhook, the state and the remedy, and reaches the wire as the `409` message through the outbox's existing `assertRedeliverAllowed` seam, which the diff does not touch. The pins assert code, status, subject, the state word and the remedy fragment rather than the whole sentence; that matches the card's statement of what the reason owes.
6. **`active` field description untouched — right.** "Inactive webhooks are skipped by the dispatcher" is now true of both paths, which is what triage directed. `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx:105` and `:562`–`:568` state the field and the door's codes without enumerating the veto's cases; nothing there reads false after this diff (prose surface: the ACCEPT's sentence-level check stands; no finding against it here).
7. **Existing pin re-aimed only where the new rule required it — right.** `webhook-system-context.pin.test.ts` gains `active: true` on its one fixture row; the pin still asserts what it is for (`findOne` under `isSystem`). The `subscriptionRow` helper in `webhook-drop-durable-record.test.ts` already defaulted `active: true` at the head, so no `#8069` pin changed meaning silently.
8. **Driver presentation of `active` (the ACCEPT's one question for this tier) — answered: every driver hands this check a JS boolean, or null.** At `origin/main`, the SQL driver's `formatOutput` runs a `[#11782]` pass that presents every registered scalar `boolean` / `toggle` column (`booleanFields[object]`, filled at schema sync) as `Boolean(v)` on SQLite and MySQL, leaving `null`/`undefined` alone; `findOne` returns through `formatOutput`; Postgres stores a real boolean that node-pg parses; the memory driver round-trips the engine-written value; MongoDB is native. A null therefore reaches the guard as null and is refused as inactive, which item 2 shows is the dispatcher's own answer for that row. Residual class, named and not a defect: the coercion is keyed to the schema-sync registry, so a table whose boolean column were missing from it would fail CLOSED here (a false "inactive" refusal of an active webhook on SQLite/MySQL, visible to the operator at the door), never open — a refusal class, not an egress class.
9. **Check-runs on the head — all completed; latest per name is `success` or `skipped`; none failed or was cancelled.** The two still running at brief time, `Test Core (3/6)` and the aggregate `Test Core`, both completed `success`. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, all four `Type Check` jobs and the six `Test Core` shards are `success`. No governed surface is in the file list; head repo equals base repo.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/22804-redeliver-inactive-veto.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks` **`patch`** — right. The card is a `bug` card (class (b): implementation contradicting declared text), and a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`. The body carries FROM → TO, the operator's one-line fix, and the statement that the gone/secret refusals are unchanged; each sentence matches the diff. `Check Changeset` is `success`.
- **`Clause-②: no`, no direction arm — right**, on the PR body line 2 and in the changeset body. The question the line answers is widening of a published accept set or public surface; this diff widens neither (no new error code — `DELIVERY_NOT_ELIGIBLE` is already in the ledger — no new export, no new accepted input). It narrows a measured accept set back to declared contract text, and the rule for that shape is `no`, in lane, owing one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review before the queue — this record. The text it is pulled back to: `sys-webhook.object.ts:179` ("Inactive webhooks are skipped by the dispatcher") under triage's reading that an explicit replay is the dispatcher. The `(narrowing)` arm is for a BREAKING narrowing of a published contract; the published door text, `IWebhookService.handleRedeliver` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/webhook-service.ts:56`–`58`), already names "the producer's veto refused it" as a `409 DELIVERY_NOT_ELIGIBLE` cause without closing the veto's case set, so no published contract is contradicted by the third case. The one sentence that could be read the other way is the same file's header rationale (`:22`–`23`, "whose subscription or signing secret is gone"); it is why-prose, not the member's contract, and it stays true for the two cases it names — so it does not move the level. Triage's `Clause-②: yes` suggestion was a conflation of "narrows" with "widens" and the claim was right to decline it.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (five, from `os-dev-report` `6109045625`), each answered:
1. Null/absent `active` refused rather than defaulted true — **accepted**; see ① items 2 and 8. The decisive evidence is the dispatcher's own predicate, which the dispatch's "declared default" reading would have contradicted for that row.
2. Branch not merged with `origin/main` before the PR — **no bearing**; the three intervening commits touch none of the five files, and every check on the head ran on CI's merge ref and is green.
3. Shallow fetch of a pinned fixture commit into the shared object store — **process note, no contract bearing**.
4. Commit/PR attribution trailer form — **outside this record's three sections**; AGENTS.md governs that spelling, and it changes nothing published.
5. Door pins assert subject, state word and remedy fragment, not the full sentence — **accepted**; the card and triage name those three facts as the reason's contract, and the status and code are pinned in full.

`open_questions`: none declared. Out-of-scope findings (two), answered:
- `packages/spec/src/contracts/webhook-service.ts:22`–`23` now names two of the veto's three cases — **incomplete, not false; not a blocker for this head.** The member's own contract text covers the new case. The ACCEPT's carrier ("the next PR that edits that file") is not a carrier; **escalated to the owning seat: name one** — a one-line `packages/spec` docblock follow-up in the spec lane, which, touching a published contract surface, takes its own record. ⛔ Not folded into this PR: the claim excluded `packages/spec` and the dev correctly left it untouched.
- `webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:415`–`418` (`installRedeliverGuard` docblock, "whose signing configuration is no longer available") and the `:438` log string — **verified present at `origin/main`; still true, narrower than the veto now is; acceptance-note class, nothing owed.**

Nothing here goes to the maintainer's decision box: triage took the product reading on the card and the diff implements exactly that reading, tightening the door and loosening nothing.

Reviewed-by: `session_013LbZ9MhPp1iriZEtgJqioA`

**VERDICT: PASS**
